Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. That is the single thread running through most Chicago electrical work.

Electrical Grounding and Bonding Services in Chicago — the practical detail

Grounding and bonding give fault current a deliberate path and keep exposed metal at the same electrical potential. We diagnose missing, loose and incorrectly connected grounding paths in Chicago properties.

What drives the cost

The City dataset has only 24 GFCI-tagged permits and no dependable standalone grounding sample, so we do not present a citywide median for this work.

Before you book anyone

  • What is the difference between grounding and bonding? — Bonding connects conductive parts together; grounding connects the system to an approved grounding electrode arrangement. Both support fault clearing and voltage stability.
  • Does a ground rod fix ungrounded outlets? — Not by itself. Branch-circuit equipment grounding and the service grounding electrode system are different parts of the installation.
  • Can a GFCI protect an ungrounded receptacle? — It can provide personnel protection when installed and labeled correctly, but it does not create an equipment ground.
  • Why are neutral and ground separated in a subpanel? — Downstream of the service disconnect, separating them helps keep normal return current off metal enclosures and grounding paths.
  • Will this need a permit? — Some corrections are minor; service or electrode work commonly requires permitting. We confirm against the exact scope.

||Infrared Electrical Inspection — Detail::

Infrared and Thermal Electrical Inspection Services in Chicago — the practical detail

Infrared scanning can reveal unusual heat patterns while equipment is operating, but the image is a clue—not a diagnosis by itself. We pair thermal observations with electrical inspection and measured load conditions.

What drives the cost

Infrared electrical inspection is not a standalone Chicago permit category. Pricing follows equipment count, access, operating load, documentation and whether shutdown coordination is required.

Before you book anyone

  • What can an infrared electrical inspection find? — It can identify temperature differences that may be associated with loose connections, imbalance, overload or component trouble, subject to electrical verification.
  • Does a bright thermal color always mean danger? — No. Palette colors are relative to the image scale. Actual temperature, load and comparison with similar components matter.
  • Does equipment need to be operating? — Usually yes. Many useful thermal anomalies appear only when current is flowing under a representative load.
  • Will I receive images or a report? — The scope can include annotated images, equipment references and recommended follow-up.
  • Does thermal scanning require a permit? — Inspection alone generally does not. Any resulting repair may have its own permit requirement.
